region.text: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire shape of 1534 inside Brazil

ledger.note: 1534: King John III divides Brazil into hereditary captaincies. 'Between 1534 and 1536 king John III divided the land into 15 captaincy colonies.' The page gives no boundaries; the coast is Cliopatria's.
1549: the General Government replaces the private captaincies. 'In 1549, Portuguese King John III abolished the system of private colonies'; Salvador is the capital (infobox 'Salvador (1549-1763)').

region.text: Guanabara Bay

ledger.note: 1555: the French found France Antarctique in Guanabara Bay. The French settlement 'was founded in 1555 in Guanabara Bay'; Mem de Sa 'waged war against the colony in 1560' and 'managed to expel the last French settlers in 1567'.

region.text: Guanabara Bay

ledger.note: 1567: the last French settlers are expelled from Guanabara Bay. Mem de Sa 'managed to expel the last French settlers in 1567'.

1580: the Iberian Union puts the Portuguese crown, and Brazil, under the Spanish Habsburgs. 'The unification of the crowns of the two Iberian kingdoms, known as the Iberian Union, lasted until 1640.' Cliopatria draws no Portuguese shape in 1582-1618.

1621: the Governorate General of Brazil becomes the State of Brazil. 'In 1621, an administrative reorganization took place, and the Governorate General of Brazil became known as the State of Brazil'; the State of Maranhao, based in Sao Luis, was separate. The Maranhao dossier (state-of-maranhao-and-grao-para) holds the north.

region.text: Recife and Olinda, Dutch Brazil

ledger.note: 1630: the Dutch take Recife and Olinda. 'From 1630 to 1654, the Dutch set up more permanently in commercial Recife and aristocratic Olinda.'

region.text: the coast from Rio Grande do Norte to Cabo de Santo Agostinho

ledger.note: 1634: the Dutch hold the coast. 'By 1634, the Dutch controlled the coastline from the Rio Grande do Norte to Pernambuco's Cabo de Santo Agostinho' (Dutch Brazil page). Mirror of dutch-brazil /ledger/1 (gain from portuguese-empire): the State of Brazil is the Portuguese state that held the coast and its Cliopatria keyframe (colonial-brazil_1630, 1630-1651) still draws it. [fx-22 2026-11-01: added as the mirror of the dutch-brazil event; the compiler gave the cells to the Dutch by the size rule (colonial-brazil with dutch-brazil, 701 cells in 1634, 1637, 1641).]

region.text: the captaincy of Ceará

ledger.note: 1637: the Dutch take Ceara. 'Within the year, Maurice of Nassau captured the captaincy of Ceara' (Dutch Brazil page; Maurice took over the GWC's command in 1637). Mirror of dutch-brazil /ledger/3; 319 of the captaincy's cells are in the State of Brazil's 1630 shape. [fx-22 2026-11-01: added as the mirror of the dutch-brazil event; the compiler gave the cells to the Dutch by the size rule (colonial-brazil with dutch-brazil, 701 cells in 1634, 1637, 1641).]
1640: the Iberian Union ends and the Portuguese crown, and Brazil, return to a separate king. The Iberian Union 'lasted until 1640'; the page does not name the Braganza dynasty.

Mirror of dutch-brazil /ledger/4: 65 of its cells (Piaui and the Pernambuco side) are in the State of Brazil's 1630 shape; the Maranhao cells belong to the State of Maranhao (see the handoff on state-of-maranhao-and-grao-para). region.text: the land Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire holds inside Brazil in 1752 and not in 1720, without the State of Maranhao: Goias, Mato Grosso, Rio Grande do Sul and the interior between (Minas Gerais, Bahia, Tocantins, Piaui, Rondonia and the rest)

ledger.note: 1750 (13 January): the Treaty of Madrid. Portugal gets 'undisputed sovereignty over the gold and diamond districts of Goias and Mato Grosso' and keeps Rio Grande do Sul on the basis of uti possidetis ('each party must stay with what it now holds'); the Amazon basin gain goes to the State of Maranhao. Spain was to receive Sacramento and Portugal the Misiones Orientales, which the Guarani War of 1756 prevented; the treaty was 'nullified' by El Pardo (1761). [fx-22 fix 2026-11-01: the region was the three whole states Goias, Mato Grosso and Rio Grande do Sul (5,876 cells, 1,143 of them outside the 1752 shape: southern Rio Grande do Sul and Mato Grosso) and left out the rest of the interior that the 1752 shape holds (Minas Gerais, Bahia, Mato Grosso do Sul, Tocantins, Rondonia, Piaui: 8,081 cells), so the 1752 keyframe snapped 8,081 cells in and 1,068 out. Treaty of Madrid page, opened 2026-11-01: Spain 'accepted Portuguese westward expansion', the treaty was based on uti possidetis ('each party must stay with what it now holds') and aimed at 'the gold and diamond districts of Goias and Mato Grosso' and 'Rio Grande do Sul'; Colonial Brazil page: 'At the end of the 17th century, the bandeirantes' expeditions discovered gold in central Brazil', the first Minas Gerais town 'created in 1711', Caete 1714, Pitangui 1715, Sao Jose do Rio das Mortes 1717, and Spain and Portugal 'agreed to a considerable Southwestward expansion of colonial Brazil' in 1750. The pages do not date the individual advances of 1700-1750, so the whole of the difference between Cliopatria's 1720 and 1752 shapes is booked at the treaty, at confidence 2; the part nobody held is the next event.]

region.text: the land Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire holds inside Brazil in 1752 and not in 1720, without the State of Maranhao: Goias, Mato Grosso, Rio Grande do Sul and the interior between (Minas Gerais, Bahia, Tocantins, Piaui, Rondonia and the rest)

ledger.note: 1750 (13 January): the interior that Portugal already held or settled between 1700 and 1750 and that no state held (the sertao of Bahia, Piaui and Minas Gerais, Tocantins and the rest of the same region as the gain above). Treaty of Madrid page: the treaty rests on uti possidetis ('each party must stay with what it now holds') and Spain 'accepted Portuguese westward expansion'; Colonial Brazil page: gold found in central Brazil at the end of the 17th century, the first Minas Gerais town 'created in 1711'. Same region as the gain from spanish-empire above: that event takes what Spain held, this one takes what nobody held. [fx-22 2026-11-01: added so that the ledger reaches the 1752 keyframe; the pages do not date the single advances.]

region.text: the land Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire holds inside Brazil in 1778 and not in 1752, without the Misiones Orientales: the western Amazon (Amazonas, Roraima, Para) and strips of Rio Grande do Sul and Mato Grosso do Sul

ledger.note: 1777: the First Treaty of San Ildefonso re-establishes the Treaty of Madrid. Treaty of Madrid page: the treaty was 'nullified by the Treaty of El Pardo' in 1761 and 'Its terms, with a few exceptions, were re-established in the First Treaty of San Ildefonso in 1777'; under Madrid Portugal was to take 'the greater part of the Amazon basin' and Spain 'accepted Portuguese westward expansion'. The region is the researcher's reading: Cliopatria draws the Portuguese Empire 5,798 cells wider inside Brazil in 1778 than in 1752. This event takes what Spain held; the next takes what nobody held. region.text: the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay river

ledger.note: 1801: Portugal keeps the Misiones Orientales. The war of 20 May-9 June 1801 included a 'Portuguese invasion of Misiones Orientales'; 'neither Spain nor Portugal returned the territories acquired in America (Eastern Missions)'.

1815 (16 December): Brazil becomes a kingdom in union with Portugal. 'Creation of United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves: 16 December 1815.' The court had arrived in Rio de Janeiro in March 1808.

ledger.note: 1821 (18 July): the Banda Oriental is annexed. An assembly of 'Oriental notables' on 18 July 1821 gave 'general acclamation'; the province was 'annexed ... into the Kingdom of Brazil under the name of Cisplatina' (after about three years of fighting in the countryside).

wars.outcome: The Dutch held Recife and Olinda from 1630 to 1654.

wars.outcome: The Guarani refused the transfer of the Misiones Orientales; the war of 1756 and the Jesuits' resistance 'led to the nullification of the treaty by the subsequent Treaty of El Pardo' (1761).

wars.name: War of the Oranges

zones.text: the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay river

wars.outcome: Badajoz (6 June 1801) and Madrid (29 September 1801): Portugal ceded Olivenza; the Misiones Orientales stayed Portuguese.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Banda Oriental

wars.outcome: Montevideo was occupied on 20 January 1817; the countryside was fought over for about three years; the province was annexed in 1821.

certainty.note: No surveyed frontiers: the coast and the Tordesillas line were never mapped; bandeirante expansion is undated.
The 1750 and 1777 lines follow rivers (Uruguay, Iguacu, Parana, Paraguay, Guapore, Madeira, Javary) but the interior was unsurveyed; the Rio Grande and Misiones frontier is sharper after 1801.

notes:
Written by am-06-x from five pages (budget 2-5). Not settled:
(1) Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire row supplies the shapes inside Brazil (it has no row for 1582-1618): 68,000 km2 in 1534, 322,000 in 1572, 1.33 M in 1720, 5.66 M in 1752 (the Madrid treaty year), 7.12 M in 1778. The page's only area (8,100,200 km2, no year) is the late extent. The bandeirante expansion, the Amazon and Mato Grosso frontier and the date of the Portuguese move into the Amazon are not on the pages; the north (Maranhao and Grao-Para, excluded from the shape in 1621-1651, 1654-1774) is the State of Maranhao and Grao-Para (a separate dossier, state-of-maranhao-and-grao-para, from 1621 to 1774; Brazil absorbs it in 1775, 'merge').
(2) Not on the pages opened: the Treaty of El Pardo's day (1761), the San Ildefonso (1 October 1777) text for Brazil (the Rio de la Plata page of the sibling dossier says Spain gave up Santa Catalina and Rio Grande; the Brazil page only says Colonia do Sacramento was 'definitively conquered' in 1777), the Portuguese invasion of French Guiana (1809-1817), the dates of the move into Mato Grosso, Goias and the Amazon. Colonia do Sacramento belongs to the portuguese-empire dossier (am-06-a), not to this one.
(3) The Misiones Orientales: Cliopatria's 1778 shape already includes them; the page-dated acquisition is 1801. The 1750 gain is dated by the treaty; the treaty was nullified in 1761 and the possession stands de facto (an interpretation, not on the page).
(4) The Cisplatina province is kept inside this dossier (1821-1822) and not given its own; the Cisplatine War (1825-1828) belongs to empire-of-brazil (am-08). The page's infobox has the Banda Oriental 'annexed to the UK of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves: 1817', its text 1821; 1821 is used.
(5) Wikipedia's Colonial Brazil covers 1500-1815; this dossier runs to the independence of 1822 so that the kingdom years 1815-1822 (no Cliopatria row after 1821) are covered. Counterparts: 'state-of-maranhao-and-grao-para' (this batch), 'dutch-brazil', 'france-antarctique' (am-06-c), 'federal-league' (am-08).
